research/musecode/config-paths.md verification C4 (tui: keymap activated; terminal_background, prompt_hint_enabled, rules_import_offer_dismissed, foreign_context_notice_shown are unknown_member) and M5 (the enterprise key registry: run has 11 of the user's 13 fields, provider_retry 3 of 4, telemetry 6 of 9, endpoint_transport 3 of 9)
research/musecode/config-paths.md §7.3 — `field_not_activated` means the field exists in the schema but its gate is off in this build; a distinct signal from wrong_type
research/experiments/loose-ends.md §3.4 — wrong_type and semantic_invalid are reported before the activation gate, so field_not_activated implies the value passed type validation

live probe 2026-09-02 against 1.0.1-R2006.1: camelCase `mcpServers` → unknown_member, snake `mcp_servers` → valid; `tui.theme` → field_not_activated; wrong_type elsewhere in the same document wins over field_not_activated regardless of key order; unknown_member and field_not_activated lines carry no location
notes: The validator reports only the FIRST problem and prints no location for unknown_member / field_not_activated on 1.0.x; since 1.3.0-R3057.1 the verdict arrives as `enterprise_document_invalid: plane=… reason=field_not_activated location=…` (same meaning, now with a location), so omm validates one touched top-level key per document: an unknown_member answer then means the validator cannot see that key at all and the load probe (`muse skills list --source user --json` against a temp config root) is the remaining oracle.

Nested members of mcp_servers entries (McpServerDefaultsV1 has 6 of the user's 13 fields) are not enumerated here; an unknown_member for a projected `mcp_servers` document is handled by the same blind rule.
